$comment: Flagged for review. Anything the site could not confirm, contradicted itself, or deliberately refused to guess. Publishing these is not a failure state — it is the gate leaving a receipt. Rows are never deleted; flip status to resolved and record the proof.

flags.title: All five submitted product IDs are 9 characters; an ASIN is 10
flags.what_we_found: B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3, B00hJ57DV, B0c8moW59, B0f3GKalj — each exactly 9 characters. Amazon defines an ASIN as “a unique 10-character alphanumeric code”, typically starting “B0”.
flags.consequence: No listing can be cited, priced, described, or linked. Every product field in the register is blank by policy, not by omission.
flags.how_to_clear: Re-copy each ID from the product page URL (the ten characters after /dp/) or use the Associates link builder, then replace the values in data/products.json and data/product-intent.json and run npm run check.

flags.title: link.amazon is not an Amazon product host and carries no tag parameter
flags.what_we_found: Product pages live at https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>; Associates tagging is a `tag=` parameter inside that link (Policy §2(a): the Associates ID must appear “as a parameter in the URL of each link”). The submitted URLs have neither.
flags.consequence: Even if the ID were well-formed, the supplied form could not be shown to attribute a click to the account, and it could not be reviewed for policy compliance.
flags.how_to_clear: Rebuild the five links inside Associates Central so the tag is embedded, then run the Link-Checker step in SG-05 before scaling to the rest of the catalogue.

flags.title: Compliance status of the supplied short links is unresolved — do not call them invalid
flags.what_we_found: The brief asks that these links not be declared invalid. Nothing here can see where they redirect, so the honest state is unknown: not valid, not invalid, unobserved.
flags.consequence: Any copy that asserted either way would be a fabrication. The site therefore prints “not observed” and leaves the redirect field empty rather than inferring a destination.
flags.how_to_clear: Open one link logged out, in a clean browser profile, record the final URL in the observation block of data/product-intent.json, and note the date. That single step moves the row from unobserved to evidence.

flags.title: The niche (air fryers / multi-function kitchen appliances) is inferred from the editorial hypotheses, not from the listings
flags.what_we_found: The brief's working titles concern air fryers and multi-function appliances. No submitted link resolves to a product, so no link confirms the cluster.
flags.consequence: Section pages publish the buyer frameworks and hold the five intake records as pending rather than filing products into sections they may not belong to.
flags.how_to_clear: Confirm the five product titles, then set each product's category in data/products.json; the build files them automatically.

flags.title: No demand data behind any headline
flags.what_we_found: Titles such as “Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?” are editorial hypotheses. There is no search-volume, click-through, or ranking data in this repository to justify a popularity claim.
flags.consequence: Copy never says “popular”, “trending”, or “most searched”. The topic-selection tool (tools/next-topics.mjs) stays empty until a Search Console export is dropped into data/exports/.
flags.how_to_clear: Verify the property in Search Console, publish for two weeks, export the Queries report, and re-run npm run topics.

flags.title: GitHub Pages cannot run the click endpoint or hold account credentials
flags.what_we_found: Pages serves committed static files. A counting endpoint and a PA-API caller both need a server and a secret store, which this host does not provide.
flags.consequence: The measurement layer ships as a tested local reference implementation plus the runbook for the host decision (Q-09). No page on this site claims that analytics are live.
flags.how_to_clear: Pick a runtime (small VPS, a worker platform, or a self-hosted Umami), point the site's data-collect-url at it, and keep the Associates credential server-side only.

sources.label: GitHub Docs — configuring a publishing source

flags.title: No conversion score, EPC, or revenue forecast is published anywhere
flags.what_we_found: The campaign ledger is empty and its columns may only be filled from authorized first-party reports. Nothing on the site projects earnings, and none of the numbers a forecast needs exist yet.
flags.consequence: A reader — or a future session — cannot mistake a modelled number for a measured one. The trade-off is that the site offers no revenue promise, which is the point.
flags.how_to_clear: Nothing to clear. It becomes meaningful when the first dated row lands from Associates Central Reports.

flags.title: The suggestion board is a menu, not an approved plan
flags.what_we_found: Thirty suggestions sit in /suggestions/ with effort, risk, and the decision each unlocks. Only the subset marked shipped or in progress has been built.
flags.consequence: Code that a session invented but nobody chose never reaches the reader-facing site without a recorded decision.
flags.how_to_clear: Tick a path (A, B, or C) on /suggestions/ and change the chosen rows' status; the board is the decision record.

flags.title: Brand name “The Preheat” is not cleared
flags.what_we_found: No trademark or collision search was run. The name also has to stay clear of Amazon's mark usage rules — the site must not imply Amazon sponsorship (Operating Agreement §5).
flags.consequence: The name is a working title used consistently across the build so it can be swapped in one file if it must change.
flags.how_to_clear: Search USPTO TESS and a general web search for the name in the publishing/review space; if clear, register the domain and update config/site.config.json.

flags.title: Bylines are a desk byline, not a person
flags.what_we_found: Guides are drafted with AI assistance and edited here. Inventing a credentialed human reviewer would be a fabricated endorsement — squarely inside what the FTC's honesty principle covers.
flags.consequence: Every article prints an honest authorship note and states that no product was tested. The page that would normally carry the byline is /editorial-standards/.
flags.how_to_clear: Name a real, consenting human editor, add their bio and review scope to data/people.json, and change config.brand.byline.

flags.title: Imagery is generated editorial illustration, not product photography or test photos
flags.what_we_found: The site's illustrations were made for this build. They are not photographs of the submitted products and are not documentation of a test kitchen.
flags.consequence: Captions say what the picture is, and no image is presented as evidence that a product was used. Product imagery from Amazon's Program Content may only be used under the license Amazon supplies (Program Content, OA §1).
flags.how_to_clear: Either keep illustrations labelled as illustrations, or shoot your own photos of the product in your kitchen — which is also the single biggest trust upgrade available (SG-16).

flags.title: Quoted policy text carries a revision date that must be re-checked at every publish
flags.what_we_found: The Operating Agreement read here is dated “Updated: October 15, 2025”. Section numbering differs across locales (the Amazon.in agreement puts the same disclosure clause at §10), so section numbers are cited with their locale.
flags.consequence: The gate stores the retrieval date with every quotation; a stale quote is a compliance bug, not a typo.
flags.how_to_clear: Re-run node tools/compliance-gate.mjs --refresh-sources monthly; it re-checks each row in data/sources.json against the live page.

flags.title: Publishing under a github.io sub-directory vs a domain you own
flags.what_we_found: Amazon's review criteria state plainly: “You must own your website.” A site at user.github.io/repo sits inside somebody else's domain, which is a foreseeable reason for an application to be rejected — and a rejection cannot be re-assessed for that application.
flags.consequence: The site is fully built so it can be deployed to a domain you control with a one-line config change; the Pages URL is treated as a staging surface, not the application asset.
flags.how_to_clear: Buy the domain, add a CNAME + custom domain in Pages settings, set config.baseUrl, rebuild, and submit that URL to Associates Central.

sources.label: GitHub Docs — custom domains for Pages

flags.title: Zero traffic, zero backlinks, zero history
flags.what_we_found: This domain/path has no index history, so there is no baseline to compare against and no ranking to promise.
flags.consequence: The plan is expressed in editorial output and measured queries rather than in projected sessions.
flags.how_to_clear: Submit the sitemap, let it crawl, and the ledger starts collecting real rows.

flags.title: No contact address, no privacy policy commitment, no newsletter storage decision
flags.what_we_found: config.contact.email is unset, and the reader-capture form in SG-30 has nowhere lawful-and-configured to send addresses. A publication that collects emails without a stated policy is worse than one that collects nothing.
flags.consequence: The signup block ships as a disabled component with a visible “not wired” note. No form on this site transmits anything.
flags.how_to_clear: Add a monitored address, choose where addresses are stored, publish a privacy page naming that processor, then set config.contact.email and flip data/forms.json enabled=true.

sources.label: Amazon — Operating Agreement §4 warranties (compliance with applicable law)

flags.title: Repo was empty: the brief's earlier artefact IDs have no backing files
flags.what_we_found: The brief references rows like SG-27..SG-30, FLG-003, S01/S07/S24 and a prior source register, but the branch history contains one commit and one file (README.md, “# WinA”).
flags.consequence: Those IDs were re-derived here rather than trusted: SG-27..SG-30 and FLG-003 exist as described, S-numbers are unmapped because no prior spec file survives to map them against.
flags.how_to_clear: If an earlier register exists in another branch or repo, drop it in data/legacy/ and re-run the build; the board will merge by ID.
